title: What Powered Work Clothing Is
definition: Powered Work Clothing: workwear with built-in powered assistance.
description:

The Signature clothing hulls program starts where public roadmaps stop. title: The Signature Vision: Powered Work Clothing
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Powered Work Clothing.

Signature clothing hulls program, charter one: master assist fibers at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale clothing logistics manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate washability systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Powered Work Clothing becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

t: 2030 — First clothing hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
title: 2030 — First clothing hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
definition: 2030 milestone on the Powered Work Clothing roadmap.
description:
First clothing hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses, farms and ergonomic fit construction sites.

What must be true first: the assist fibers results have to replicate outside the lab, clothing logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and washability operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed assist fibers demonstrations, clothing logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting washability uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Powered Work Clothing
definition: Estimates Powered Work Clothing readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Powered Work Clothing components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a clothing hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

definition: Simulates Powered Work Clothing operating for a day.
description:

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where assist fibers monitoring, clothing logistics redundancy, or washability maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Powered Work Clothing Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Powered Work Clothing: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Powered Work Clothing — workwear with built-in powered assistance.

Phase 1 — Prove (assist fibers): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (clothing logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (washability): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (ergonomic fit): clothing hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and industry-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
